title:
Rehabilitation for Oleksandr
Helping a Father Use His Hand Again
subtitle: A Ukrainian veteran relearning how to hold a fork, button a shirt, and rebuild an ordinary life
location: Way to Health Rehabilitation Centre, Dnipro, Ukraine

intro.quote: Not every battle ends when the fighting stops. Some begin only after the explosions fall silent.
paragraphs: This is Oleksandr. Since 2022 he has served in the infantry, defending Ukraine on some of the most dangerous front lines. Today, the hardest enemy he faces is no longer on the battlefield.

timeline.heading: A quiet life, and everything that mattered
paragraphs: Before the war, Oleksandr lived a simple, peaceful life in a small Ukrainian village. He wasn't chasing success or adventure.

His greatest happiness was waiting for him at home — his wife and their two children. The ordinary moments most of us barely notice were everything to him: time spent together, family dinners, watching his children grow up.

images.alt: Oleksandr with his wife and their two children

timeline.heading: An impossible choice
paragraphs: Like so many Ukrainian fathers, Oleksandr made an impossible choice. He put on a military uniform — not because he wanted to leave his family, but because he wanted to protect the future they deserved.
Since 2022 he has served in the infantry, defending Ukraine on some of the most dangerous front lines.

images.alt: Oleksandr in military uniform during his service

timeline.heading: In a single moment, everything changed
paragraphs: During a combat mission between Chasiv Yar and Stupochky, a thermobaric drone munition exploded nearby. The blast left him with devastating injuries.
But the injury that changed his life most was to his left arm.
list: Shrapnel wounds to his face and eyes
Left arm: multiple fractures, nerve damage and bone loss
Shrapnel tearing through muscles and joints

timeline.heading: The hardest enemy is no longer on the battlefield
paragraphs: Before starting rehabilitation at Way to Health, Oleksandr was asked to perform one very simple task in the rehabilitation kitchen: to cut food, to hold a knife, to use a fork. Something millions of people do every day without giving it a second thought.
For Oleksandr, it became one of the hardest things he had ever tried to do. Every movement required incredible concentration. Pain. Patience. And determination. Yet he never gave up.

images.alt: Oleksandr attempting to cut food in the rehabilitation kitchen
Close-up of Oleksandr's hands during the cutting task

rehab.title: How the Rehabilitation Works
rehab.description: At Way to Health, a multidisciplinary team is walking this journey beside Oleksandr. Step by step, they are helping him regain strength, movement and confidence as he works towards using his left arm again and returning to everyday life.

goals.title: Rehabilitation Goals
goals.shortTerm: Increase the range of motion of the joints of the left upper limb.
goals.longTerm: Restore functional use of the left upper limb and regain independence in daily activities.
